content:
alex: Anyone else see the retention compaction run spike CPU on exporter pods last night? p99 for exporter-service jumped ~3x over the normal window. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/servers/telemetry?panel=exporter_cpu

maya: Yup. I saw a correlated rise in encoder allocs and heap from the proto path. Looks attribute-heavy spans triggered a lot of work.

simon: My suspicion is attribute indexing + map allocations per-span. The retention path parses and re-encodes spans (proto) which can blow up allocs if we build maps for every span.

emma: Did a quick local repro — encode 1000 spans (avg 60 attrs) through retention pipeline: allocs ~18k, elapsed 1.2s. Skipping attr-indexing (short-circuit) drops allocs to ~3k and elapsed to 0.3s.

alex: Important note: retention job intentionally rewrites traces for storage (normalization + tagging), so exporter encoder is hot in that path.

maya: Pasting the relevant logs from the canary run:

```text
2026-03-19T03:12:08Z exporter.go:256 encodeSpan batch=512 attrs=74 allocs=18243 cpu_ms=1234
2026-03-19T03:12:08Z encoder/proto allocs=17200 heap_mb=45
2026-03-19T03:12:08Z retention.compactor spans_rewritten=120000 duration_ms=250000
```

simon: Short term mitigations: 1) lower batch size for retention rewrite, 2) add a shared KV key pool / dedupe keys before building full maps, 3) change proto encoder to reuse buffers and object pools. Also consider a fast-path for retention-only mode that skips full attribute indexing when not needed.

emma: I prototyped a buffer pool + proto encoder reuse patch — local bench shows ~70% alloc reduction and ~2.5x faster encode. I'll open a PR with benchmarks and a small repro harness.

otel-bot: Retention-job #457 started at 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z (canary cluster)

alex: Can we get that patch on a canary exporter and run the retention canary tomorrow before next full run? We need to avoid another spike.

maya: :thumbsup: EMMA, please include detailed before/after numbers in PR and a runbook step to flip pool on/off.

emma: PR: https://github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/789 — includes benchmark harness, a repro script, and a config flag `exporter.reuse_buffers = true`.

simon: Note: verify p99 tail latencies under parallel load when pooling is enabled. Pooling can sometimes cause contention affecting p99 if not sized correctly.

maya: I'll schedule a brief load test on the dedicated canary cluster early tomorrow and loop in @eng-sre for the resource window.

alex: Thanks — let's keep this thread for rollout coordination. If the canary looks good, we can include the change in the next maintenance window.
